column3: It exactly repeats God's knowledge of what lies before and behind them, adding that they cannot encompass His knowledge.
It turns the before-and-behind horizon into a warning that calls people to reverence and mercy.
It exactly repeats that all matters return to God and grounds this return in His possession of heaven and earth.
It exactly repeats the comprehensive knowledge formula within the angelic setting and shows its effect on their intercession and fear.
The immediately preceding selection of angelic and human messengers supplies the referent for the focus's encompassing knowledge.
It assigns the final disposition of an affair to God rather than the messenger, clarifying the return of matters to Him.
It repeats the return of all matters while grounding it in God's kingship, though that return is already stated exactly above.
Its barriers before and behind form a contrary image of a field closed to perception.
God's sufficient knowledge supports the focus's divine knowledge only in general terms.
It repeats the return of matters to God in the context of prophets being denied, adding a messenger-facing application.
The following command to worship and do good supplies a local human response to the divine authority just stated.
It places a completed military affair and its outcome under the same return of all matters to God.
It joins the completion of the affair to the exact return formula, giving the return an eschatological judicial setting.
The exclusion of falsehood from before and behind gives a distinct protected-front-and-rear counterpart.
Its contrast between parables and those who understand does not materially develop divine knowledge or the return of matters.
It repeats the knowledge formula and sets it within God's living sovereignty, permitted intercession, and unburdensome preservation.
The adjacent conclusion makes the chosen community and messenger witnesses, extending the local messenger setting into communal responsibility.
It places watchers before and behind a chosen messenger, concretizing a protected mission field around messengers.
It offers a contrary reading in which companions beautify what lies before and behind people before their loss is confirmed.
It names what lies before, behind, and between angels as belonging to God, directly linking the phrase to commanded descent and unfailing remembrance.
Its confession of belonging to God and returning to Him gives the focus's return a lived response to loss.
God's knowledge of what is concealed and disclosed provides a close, distinct expression of comprehensive knowledge.
The protected Book has a limited connection to the message environment but does not state the focus's knowledge or return.
It declares that the whole affair belongs to God and that He knows inner states, applying both themes in a crisis.
Its spatial before-and-behind view of heaven and earth is a remote counterpart to the focus's comprehensive horizon.
Turning away from signs is only a contrary response within the broader messenger setting.
Its phrase about what lies before concerns prior scripture, with only a remote link to the focus's return scene.
It contrasts public and hidden things under God's knowledge, offering a compact parallel to His encompassing awareness.
God hears secret counsel and has messengers record it, giving a concrete messenger-mediated instance of comprehensive knowledge.
Its warning that many do not know adds only a general epistemic contrast.
The adversary's approach from before and behind supplies a contrary, four-directional use of the focus's horizon imagery.
Hard hearts and beautified deeds provide a distant contrary to a rightly received divine message.
A matter decreed by God supports divine governance but not the focus's particular knowledge or return.
It expands God's knowledge across heaven, earth, secrets, disclosures, and inner selves.
The taking of hearing and sight does not add to the focus's knowledge-and-return formulation.
It assures the messenger that God knows both their concealed and public speech.
Its before-and-behind relation describes the lesson's temporal reach, not divine knowledge of the two horizons.
Resolute patience and forgiveness do not materially clarify the focus.
It directly states that God knows what people conceal and disclose, though this repeats earlier secrecy parallels.
God's knowledge and wisdom in a social judgment are too general to add much after the stronger knowledge parallels.
It shows God's measured knowledge of hidden gestation and change, adding a developmental instance of comprehensive knowledge.
Divine all-knowledge secures prior clarification, but the verse has no close before-and-behind or return relation.
Its knowledge of entering, leaving, descending, and ascending gives a dynamic boundary-crossing parallel to the focus's encompassing knowledge.
Sharing Moses's affair with Aaron does not clarify God's knowledge or the return of all matters.
It combines God's knowledge of people's present state with their return, report of deeds, and universal knowledge.
The instantaneous divine command offers only a broad connection to God's governance of affairs.
Recognition and denial of God's favor does not materially develop the focus's central claims.
Its refusal to give angels or prophets lordship broadly guards God's ultimate authority over messengers.
Worldly surface knowledge and heedlessness of the Hereafter do not closely develop the focus.
Deferred knowledge supplies only a general future-awareness counterpart.
It unites the unseen of heaven and earth, the return of every affair to God, and His awareness of human deeds.
Messengers before and behind a people frame warning as a continuous prophetic horizon.
It rejects any attempt to instruct God because His knowledge encompasses heaven, earth, and everything.
God's superior knowledge of the guided and astray has only a general relation to the focus's comprehensive knowledge.
Guardians before and behind a person provide a concrete protective counterpart to the focus's front-and-rear scope.
The nearby account of life stages and declining knowledge gives a limited local contrast to divine comprehensive knowledge.
It names the ultimate outcome of matters as belonging to God, a close variation on their return to Him.
It links worship of the Creator with the hearers' return to Him, translating the return into a reason for devotion.
Messengers coming before and behind a people give a distinct prophetic use of the focus's directional language.
A soul's knowledge of what it brought is a limited accountability counterpart rather than God's encompassing knowledge.
It states that all matters proceed to God while grounding that movement in His ownership of heaven and earth.
Pharaoh's denial that he and his forces would return to God presents the focus's return as the error pride suppresses.
God's knowledge of what people hide and disclose closely reinforces His all-encompassing awareness.
The promise of a knowing son does not develop the focus's divine knowledge or return.
God's knowledge encompasses heaven, earth, every private gathering, and the eventual report of deeds.
The bodily phrase between hands and feet is unrelated to the focus's before-and-behind horizon.
It makes sacred institutions signs that God knows all in heaven and earth and everything besides.
The brief command to reverence does not materially clarify the focus.
God's knowledge of the unseen and seen is joined to His final judgment among servants.
God's knowledgeable witnessing of revelation and the angels' witness develops the messenger and knowledge setting.
It relates scripture to what precedes it and makes the shared return to God the setting for disclosure of disputes.
The calf's inability to return speech or control harm and benefit does not clarify the focus's return of all matters.
God's swift accounting after knowledgeable dispute has a broad judicial relation only.
Inability to go forward or return gives a limited literal echo of direction and return.
Moses's return and his people's succession are narrative events, not the focus's theological return of affairs.
It pairs God's knowledge of the unseen in heaven and earth with His sight of deeds.
Only God knowing the full succession of earlier peoples gives a limited historical form of comprehensive knowledge.
Deferring knowledge of their stay to the Lord is a narrow temporal application of superior divine knowledge.
Not going ahead of God and His messenger uses a different directional idiom and adds little after the messenger parallels.
God's exclusive judgment and the return to Him give a compact parallel to the focus's final clause.
Its reference to what preceded the Quran concerns scriptural confirmation rather than the focus's encompassing knowledge.
God's hearing and knowledge support reliance in temptation but do not add a close structural parallel.
God's judgment of disputes on the Day of Resurrection develops the final settlement of matters with Him.
Power to restore a person is only a broad, ambiguous counterpart to the focus's return.
It distinguishes human examination from God's fuller knowledge of faith and places legal decisions under His judgment.
It joins return to God with disclosure of deeds, applying final accountability within family pressure.
God's future judgment of competing claims gives a judicial instance of matters being returned to Him.
Return to the Lord after death gives the focus's final clause an explicit personal and eschatological form.
Knowledge and harmful learning appear in a long account without closely developing divine comprehensive knowledge or return.
The isolated announcement that they will know does not add to the focus.
The nearby instruction leaves disputation to God's superior knowledge of what people do, extending the local divine evaluation.
Life, death, gathering, and human ignorance present a staged account of the final return and judgment.
Preferring worldly life to the Hereafter does not itself develop the focus's claims.
The Lord's superior knowledge of an uncertain number is a narrow instance of knowledge beyond human dispute.
Patience, forgiveness, and praise at two times do not materially clarify the focus.
God knows deeds by day, takes people at night, raises them again, and brings them back for report.
The command to disperse after prayer does not develop the focus's knowledge or return.
The Lord's better knowledge of corrupters is a general instance of hidden moral discernment.
The revival sign yields recognition of God's power, only indirectly supporting the return and comprehensive knowledge themes.
Its rule for leaving a collective affair does not materially clarify the focus's divine knowledge or return.
The local declaration that God knows all in heaven and earth gives an immediate, explicit parallel to the focus's comprehensive knowledge.
God's exclusive knowledge of the unseen supplies the premise for the focus's claim that the messengers' horizons are known.
It completes the guarded-messenger passage by saying God encompasses what is with them and counts every thing, directly developing the focus's messenger-bound knowledge.
God's firstness and lastness, outwardness and inwardness, and knowledge of everything broaden the focus's temporal and comprehensive scope.
God knows what enters and leaves the earth and what descends and rises, a dynamic counterpart to His knowledge across all boundaries.
The turning of night into day and day into night ends with God's knowledge of what is within breasts, joining cosmic transition and inward knowledge.
After protective guardians and death, people are returned to God as their true Master, giving the focus's return a concrete accountability setting.
The return of all to God is joined to His true promise, creation, and recompense, expanding the focus's final clause eschatologically.
God begins creation, repeats it, and then people are returned to Him, linking return to the full created cycle.
God alone knows the Hour, rain, the womb, tomorrow's earning, and place of death, providing a concentrated account of knowledge beyond human horizons.
God's knowledge of the unseen and witnessed gives a broad but direct formulation of the comprehensive knowledge named in the focus.
The Knower of the unseen misses nothing in heaven or earth, making the focus's encompassing knowledge explicit at every scale.
It assigns disputed matters to God's judgment and directs trust and turning to Him, developing the return of affairs into a judicial orientation.
God's knowledge of the soul's whisper and nearness to the human being gives an intimate form of the focus's all-encompassing knowledge.
God's knowledge of the unseen and witnessed supplies a concise, comprehensive parallel to the focus's knowledge of every horizon.
It states that God's knowledge has encompassed everything, an explicit universal formulation that directly supports the focus.
Whether speech is concealed or public, God knows what is within breasts, extending the focus's knowledge to hidden inward action.
